h1: AI Product Content by Industry, Picked for What You Sell
lead: AI product content by industry starts with the category you sell in. One photo can become a still or a clip with a script, an actor, a voice, captions, and music.
card: Picture and clip ideas matched to what you sell.

AI images for small online shops
intro: Open the category of the item in your hand. The page shows the moment shoppers expect, then you make a still or a clip from one photo.
A clip can include an AI script, an AI actor, a voice, captions, and a track from the music library. Publish it to TikTok or Meta, or download the file.

faq.q: Which category should I open first?
faq.a: Open the category of the product you are listing. If you sell more than one kind of item, finish this one, then open the next category.

faq.q: Can I start from a phone photo?
faq.a: Yes. Use one clear photo with the whole item visible. Daylight and a plain surface make the color and shape easier to check.

faq.q: How is this different from the template library?
faq.a: These pages group ideas by what you sell. The template library groups them by layout, such as a try-on or a white background. Open a category to see the moments, then a template to make that layout.

faq.q: Can one photo become both a still and a clip?
faq.a: Yes. Upload the same photo on the category page and choose a picture template or a clip template. Each job shows its credit cost before it starts.

faq.q: Do these pages tell me the ad size for each channel?
faq.a: Channel sizes live on the platform pages. Category pages focus on the selling moment. A clip can be 9:16, 1:1, 16:9, 4:3, or 3:4.

faq.q: Will the file keep my product's color and shape?
faq.a: The file is built from the photo you upload, so start with a picture that already shows the real color and the full shape. Check the result before you post it.

faq.q: What should a new product show first?
faq.a: Show the moment a shopper uses to decide: texture for a jar, fit for a garment, a pour for a drink, or the item turned on for a gadget.

faq.q: Can I run these files as paid ads?
faq.a: Yes. Downloads can be used commercially and have no watermark. The clip can include an AI voice, captions, and music from the library. Type the price yourself. Do not state a claim the product cannot support.

faq.q: Can the clip include a voice and captions?
faq.a: Yes. Ask for an AI actor, a spoken line, and captions. Edit them in the built-in editor. The actor is not a customer.

faq.q: Can I publish from the category page?
faq.a: You make the file from the category, then publish it to TikTok or Meta in one click, or download it. Budget and audience stay in the ad account.

faq.q: Can I start this category from a product link?
faq.a: Yes. Paste a public product page. The main image and the name start the job. You still pick the template for the moment shoppers expect.

faq.q: Can I make several versions of one item?
faq.a: Yes. Run a batch from the same photo when you want another scene or another actor. Each job shows its credit cost first.

reviews.h2: How Shops in a Category Use It
reviews.lead: Examples of the job, not quotes from named customers.

items.d: A skincare shop starts from the jar photo, shows the texture, and adds a spoken line about one real use.
An apparel shop puts the garment on a generated person. The picture does not replace the size chart.
A gadget shop asks for one motion, such as a lid opening, and puts the feature name in the captions.
A food shop shows the pour or the first sip, with music under the clip and the price typed to match the listing.
A home shop places the product in a room from the photo it already has, then checks the color against the real item.
An agency runs a batch from one client photo: another actor, another opening, another frame.
